items: #1 Janice STFU: An early version was previewed on a livestream on 4 September 2025 under the title 'That's Just How I Feel' and later repurposed for the album. [wikipedia]
#5 National Treasures: An earlier version leaked on 5 November 2025 with a guest verse from Pressa. [songfacts]
#9 Make Them Pay: The song was first previewed on May 14, 2026, in the fourth episode of Drake's Iceman livestream series, a day before release. [wikipedia]
#10 What Did I Miss?: The song was premiered at the end of the 'Iceman: Episode 1' livestream, which moved into a live performance of it. [wikipedia]
#12 All The Way: The snippet teased on February 14, 2025 was a rough demo; production and both vocals were reworked afterwards. [songfacts]
#13 Evil J0rdan: Previewed on Instagram on December 8, 2023 and first released there on January 15, 2024, fourteen months before the album version. [wikipedia]
#14 Rather Lie: The song existed and was performed live three months before release, at Rolling Loud Miami on December 15, 2024. [wikipedia]
#17 4X4: The infobox gives 2024 as the recording year; the song was already being played publicly on September 22, 2024, four months before its release. [wikipedia]

#35 Cinderella: Snippets leaked in late 2023 under the alternate name 'Family Forever', with fan versions filling unfinished parts using AI, so the song existed in unfinished form months before release. [wikipedia]
#38 Enough (Miami): A snippet was first played at a club on New Year's Day, before the March release. [wikipedia]
#44 Lovin On Me: A snippet circulated on TikTok before release (Songfacts says October 2023, Wikipedia says November 2023); infobox gives 2023 as recording year and pop rap as genre. [wikipedia]
#58 Favorite Song: A snippet went up on TikTok on January 7, 2023, before release; Toosii tied a Valentine's Day release to 100,000 pre-saves. [wikipedia]
#60 Search & Rescue: Previewed on Instagram on March 25, 2023 under the working title 'Rescue Me'; the full track premiered March 31 on Drake's SiriusXM show. [wikipedia]
#62 Just Wanna Rock: Recorded in 2022; the snippet was first teased on TikTok in mid-September 2022, about a month before the October 17 release. [songfacts]
#75 Vegas: A one-minute version was teased on YouTube on April 15, 2022, and a longer snippet was performed at Coachella two days later, before the May 6 release. [songfacts]
#77 Super Freaky Girl: A snippet titled 'Freaky Girl' was previewed on July 13, 2022 and became popular on TikTok before the August 12 release. [wikipedia]

#1 Janice STFU: The instrumental came from a March 2026 session between Rogét Chahayed and FnZ, with B4U adding finishing touches. This sits oddly with the September 2025 preview date on the same … [wikipedia]
#6 Make Them Cry: The father's later recovery statement suggests the cancer line was written earlier, during the diagnosis. [songfacts]
#11 Outside: Cardi B said she made the song months before release while angry and later changed some bars. [wikipedia]
#19 TV Off: Mustard says the first-half beat came from the same line of work as "Not Like Us". [songfacts]
#21 Wacced Out Murals: Barrera recorded without knowing how her mariachi-style vocal would be used; she was asked for her own style and voice. [songfacts]
#21 Wacced Out Murals: She learned that her voice opens the track a few weeks after the session, from a friend's text. [songfacts]
#22 Hey Now: Ty Dolla Sign recorded a version over the beat that was never released (Wikipedia). Songfacts instead lists him among those who passed on it. [wikipedia]
#29 Not Like Us: Mustard's concept for the beat was Dr. Dre working with Lil Jon. [wikipedia]
#31 Family Matters: Because the 'Push Ups' outro already used this song's opening beat, journalists concluded the song's concept was prepared in advance. [wikipedia]
#32 7 Minute Drill: Cole wrote from a one-word prompt, 'light', which T-Minus picked from his workstation screen. [wikipedia]
#34 Type Shit: Metro Boomin was still mixing the track in early January 2024. [wikipedia]
#35 Cinderella: The song was initially thought to be an outtake from Travis Scott's album Utopia. [wikipedia]
#39 Carnival: West heard the track in Las Vegas, then recorded his verse and changed the melody; he added much of the production. [wikipedia]
#39 Carnival: The beat has hi-hats, which West had not wanted on the album; Ty Dolla Sign hesitated to play it for him for that reason. [wikipedia]
#39 Carnival: Ty Dolla Sign recorded his part after Rich the Kid in the same sessions. [wikipedia]
#39 Carnival: Video surfaced of West recording his verse in a room surrounded by dozens of friends. [wikipedia]
#43 Agora Hills: The track existed as an audio file by early April 2023, more than five months before release. [wikipedia]
#44 Lovin On Me: Oz's contribution changed the direction of the beat. [songfacts]
#47 Virginia Beach: 40 and Harley Arsenault played the keys and drums themselves; the production is described as soft and skittering. [songfacts]
#56 Barbie World: Minaj rejected several earlier demos and joined only on this beat, citing how the sample was used and the drums. [wikipedia]
#61 Players: It came out of a session with Goldstein, WorldWideFresh and Feli Ferraro after 80 minutes spent on a different song that did not work. [songfacts]
#64 Rich Flex: Recorded 2021-2022 at The Chapel in Toronto. [wikipedia]
#73 Forever: Lil Baby's brief for the beat was a kick and a snare, simple, with few hi-hats. [songfacts]
#73 Forever: Bizness Boi and Fortune helped build the beat, and the first attempt was accepted. [songfacts]
#79 Jimmy Cooks: Recorded in 2022. Wikipedia also says the song was first planned for Her Loss and did not make the final cut. [wikipedia]
#81 N95: Songfacts says both the bridge and the first half of the third verse were originally written for Baby Keem's 'Vent'. [songfacts]
#81 N95: Boi-1da says the beat ideas were made together in a Los Angeles studio session and Lamar then finished and assembled the song on his own. [songfacts]
#88 First Class: Chahayed (keys) and Lopez (drums) worked in the studio with Harlow throughout the album sessions. [songfacts]
#88 First Class: Harlow's stated production aim for the album was that songs keep developing musically as they go, to hold the listener. [songfacts]
#89 Big Energy: The lyrics were written as a group conversation in the room with the beat playing aloud, not written down privately. [songfacts]
#90 Do We Have A Problem?: Minaj decided to add Lil Baby as soon as she first heard the beat. [wikipedia]
#90 Do We Have A Problem?: Minaj said she wanted to write mixtape-style bars again. [wikipedia]
#91 Pushin P: Wheezy originated the beat, one of seven he made for the album. [songfacts]
#93 Way 2 Sexy: Using the Right Said Fred sample was Future's idea. [songfacts]
#94 Girls Want Girls: OZ made the beat together with Ambezza, described as his assistant. [songfacts]
#1 Janice STFU: Chahayed first heard the final version on the Iceman livestream and only learned of the interpolation from listeners online. [songfacts]
#19 TV Off: The second-half beat was originally made for a separate theatrical album Mustard was planning; he sent it to Lamar to see if he would like it. [songfacts]
#29 Not Like Us: Mustard was not in the studio for the vocals and first heard the finished song when the public did. [songfacts]
#29 Not Like Us: The beat started from sample ideas Sean Momberger sent to Mustard. [songfacts]
#29 Not Like Us: Mustard sent the beat to Lamar in a batch; Lamar and Sounwave then finished the track. [songfacts]
#29 Not Like Us: The finished beat was sent to Lamar on April 6, 2024; the infobox dates the recording to early May 2024. [wikipedia]
#80 Sticky (Drake): Gordo came up with the beat on a plane, texted Drake, and played it for him at Drake's house. [songfacts]
#93 Way 2 Sexy: Future picked the beat from 15 to 20 that TM88 played him in one night. [songfacts]
#95 Fair Trade: Oz made the beat at home in Switzerland in summer 2021 and sent it to Drake in a beat pack. [songfacts]
#95 Fair Trade: Drake returned an idea within days and the track was developed by exchanging files back and forth. [songfacts]
#5 National Treasures: For the album version, Pressa's verse was replaced by the beat switch and more Drake rapping; Pressa kept a writing credit. [songfacts]
#12 All The Way: Zimmerman did not write on the song; BigXthaPlug texted him a demo and asked him to get on it, and he recorded his vocal afterwards. [wikipedia]
#12 All The Way: Zimmerman recorded his part separately and sent it back. [songfacts]
#33 Like That: An earlier version of the song had only Future on vocals; that is what Rodney-O was sent for clearance, without Lamar's verse. [wikipedia]
#46 IDGAF: Drake's verse was added later to the existing record, recorded with his engineer Noel Cadastre. [songfacts]
#56 Barbie World: Ice Spice wrote to picture: she was shown a 20-minute snippet of the film at a late-night studio session and then sent her verses. [wikipedia]
#57 All My Life: The song existed before the guest was chosen; Durk decided only J. Cole or Kanye West could take the second verse. [songfacts]
#60 Search & Rescue: An earlier version had a Lil Durk verse where Drake's second verse now sits; it leaked on June 11, 2023. [wikipedia]
#63 Superhero (Heroes & Villains): The Future part began as a separate track featuring Lil Double 0 that leaked on May 6, 2021; Chris Brown's part was added later. [songfacts]
#63 Superhero (Heroes & Villains): Chris Brown's section was a later addition. [songfacts]
#76 Tomorrow 2: Cardi B was recruited by CMG for the guest verse after she praised 'F.N.F.'. [songfacts]

#22 Hey Now: Mustard shopped the beat to other artists before Lamar; YG and Quavo turned it down. [wikipedia]
